topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's learning objectives and provides an overview of cancer hallmarks and progression models.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and signaling pathway deregulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells achieve self-sufficiency in growth signals and resist inhibitory signals through mutations in Wnt/beta-catenin, receptor tyrosine kinase, and TGF-beta pathways.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how genetic mutations arrest normal cell maturation in both hematopoietic malignancies and colorectal carcinoma.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis and cell death regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how cancer cells resist programmed cell death through alterations in p53 signaling and the balance of Bcl-2 family proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, telomere biology, and senescence bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how normal cells encounter replicative senescence via telomere shortening and how cancer cells bypass this barrier and p53-mediated stress responses by activating telomerase.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce complex cancer hallmarks and explore how tumor cells alter cellular metabolism through aerobic glycolysis, global metabolic rewiring, and oncometabolite-producing Krebs cycle mutations.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the angiogenic switch and mechanisms by which developing tumors stimulate new blood vessel growth to sustain oxygen and nutrient delivery.

topics.label: Mechanisms, barriers, and genetics of cancer metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the multi-step metastatic cascade, including circulatory dissemination, circulating tumor cell monitoring, seed-and-soil inefficiencies, and genomic duplication in metastatic clones.

topics.label: Summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by summarising the hallmarks framework and outlining practical sessions.
